title: Bangladesh anti-rape campaign centered at Shahbagh, including the Dhaka–Noakhali long march and later Shahbagh action
location: Dhaka (Shahbagh/PMO route); long-march route through Narayanganj, Cumilla, Feni and Maizdi, Noakhali
scope: Campaign with a large planned long-march phase and later localized follow-up
organizer: Progressive student and women’s groups under anti-rape campaign banners; long-march group reported in contemporary coverage
participants_original: Around 400 at the long march departure / around 450 at Shahbagh (Daily Star copy of UNB); around 400 (TBS); about 500 (New Age). These are estimates at a later campaign action, not a count for 5 October.
threshold_50_evidence: Contemporary sources place roughly 400–500 marchers at Shahbagh on 16 October; the first qualifying gathering date at campaign onset is not established.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The later long-march phase documents around 400–500 attendees; this supports scale during the campaign, not onset-specific attendance.

demands.summary: Sources describe gender-based violence policy demands, a nine-point action list and a Home Minister resignation; the demands target Bangladesh authorities.

start_date.summary: Reports on 21 October say programmes were underway from 5 October; no earlier date is assigned.

location.summary: Shahbagh in Dhaka; organized long-march route to Noakhali with reported stops/incident in Feni.

state_response.summary: Police blocked a Shahbagh-to-PMO march, barred the October long march at Feni/Shantinagar in other actions, and account of response at Feni conflict; no arrests or killings established.

notes: Contemporary reporting traces Shahbagh programmes from 5 October through at least 21 October. The planned long march ran 16–17 October. Its crowd at the later march establishes a 50+ gathering during the campaign, but the first date with 50+ participants is not established. Do not count each article/day as a separate event. Feni incident reports conflict: protesters allege an assault involving ruling-party members and police inaction; officials describe a scuffle and police intervention. No confirmed state beating or protester violence.
open_questions: Did the campaign have a qualifying 50+ crowd on 5 October itself?
Was there a long enough break to code the 16–17 October march or 21 October blockade as a separate protest action?
Did the campaign continue after 21 October, and when did it end?

title: Left alliance procession for jute-mill workers and public-sector mill demands
location: Shahbagh toward the Prime Minister’s Office, Dhaka
threshold_50_evidence: The articles document a procession and police obstruction but report no number or qualitative threshold.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No crowd count or clearly supported qualitative 50-person threshold in the opened reports.

demands.summary: Demands addressed closure/modernization, arrears and wage policy at state-owned jute mills and were directed toward the PMO.

start_date.summary: A same-day report fixes 5 October. Search results indicate earlier related activity, but an initial qualifying onset is unresolved.

location.summary: Shahbagh procession aimed at the PMO; police stopped it.

state_response.summary: Police obstruction and scuffle reported; no supported arrests or injuries count.

notes: DLA marched toward the PMO over closure of government-owned jute mills, arrears and minimum wage. The Daily Star credits UNB; those two articles share the written origin. Prior jute protest activity in September creates an episode-start question.
open_questions: Find a contemporaneous attendance estimate for 5 October.
Resolve whether the action belongs to an earlier jute-mill closure campaign and any later continuation.

title: Islami Andolan Bangladesh march on the French Embassy with explicit Bangladesh-government policy demands
location: Baitul Mukarram toward Shantinagar / French Embassy, Dhaka
participants_original: New Age reports thousands; Al Jazeera reports police estimated more than 40,000 participants; exact scale is disputed and counts are not assigned a precise bound.
threshold_50_evidence: Both New Age and Al Jazeera report thousands, while Al Jazeera attributes >40,000 to a police estimate; every source supports a crowd well above 50.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: New Age says thousands; Al Jazeera records a police estimate exceeding 40,000.

demands.summary: The source records an official Bangladesh protest, parliamentary motion, and removal of ambassador, which target the domestic state’s policy.

start_date.summary: Both body reports identify a march on 27 October.

location.summary: Dhaka; march blocked at Shantinagar before embassy.

state_response.summary: Police barricaded and stopped the march before it reached the embassy; Al Jazeera describes police action as peaceful. No arrest, accommodation or injury evidence.

notes: The march opposed Macron’s statements and French cartoons, but contemporaneous reporting also records explicit demands on Bangladesh to lodge an official protest, condemn France in Parliament, or remove the French ambassador. The October 27 march is recorded separately from the different Hifazat-led event on 2 November. Al Jazeera describes the march as peaceful; no other violence is alleged.
open_questions: Independent reviewer should determine whether participant estimates and home-state policy demands support inclusion under the source manual.
Assess episode separation from the 2 November Hifazat-led demonstration.
